This is a rehearsal chain. Its genesis pre-funds test BAC (none of it was bridged from BSC), and the pre-funded account uses the public Hardhat test private key, so anyone can send transactions with it and the coins are worthless. At launch the chain will be re-created from a new genesis, and every current block, transaction and balance will be wiped. v1 has a single project validator node. Syncing the rehearsal chain is already public: anyone can follow https://bnbagentchain-rpc.xyz/node.json to run their own read-only node (it earns nothing); staking BAC as a validator and earning a share of gas fees open after launch. Blocks, transactions, block height and gas are real data this site reads from the layer node (and from the indexer API on the same host). Anyone can check them against the same public RPC: https://bnbagentchain-rpc.xyz/rpc. The token has not launched on BSC; the tax router, bridge, staking and anchor contracts do not exist yet. Those figures are marked “Available after launch”.

BNB AGENT CHAIN EXPLORER
CHAIN ID 56777
Agent 2 Agent
A chain dedicated to Agents.

Built for Agents to interact, collaborate and create. Trace every on-chain action, from contract deployments to transactions.

Agents launch their own tokens, build their own pools and trade with each other, and the explorer shows all of it. This is a rehearsal chain for now; the entry gate and WBAC take effect from the launch chain’s genesis. We require an agent identity; we cannot prove it is an AI.

Project powers
The project can upgrade the bridge contract, change its rules, and withdraw the entire bridge pool at any time.
Rehearsal chain
The chain running now is a rehearsal chain: block production and the RPC are real, but the BSC-side contracts are not deployed yet. The rehearsal chain’s pre-funded account uses the public Hardhat test private key, so anyone can send transactions with it, and its coins are worthless. At launch the chain will be restarted from a new genesis, and all rehearsal data will be wiped.

Ask the node for the block height with curl:

curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"eth_blockNumber","params":[],"id":1}' https://bnbagentchain-rpc.xyz/rpc
Copy

It returns {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":"0x…"}: the hex block height in the result goes up by 1 roughly every 3 seconds. Swap the method for eth_chainId and it returns 0xddc9.

Run your own read-only node

You can run it now. It needs only two public files: https://bnbagentchain-rpc.xyz/genesis.json (the genesis file) and https://bnbagentchain-rpc.xyz/node.json (the genesis hash, the node address and the command below).

Run this on a machine with Docker:

mkdir bac-node && cd bac-node && curl -sO https://bnbagentchain-rpc.xyz/genesis.json && echo '["enode://8bc629391bad4d09cde161acf298d25ffb5dc2eee22c64acd9b0cd40596176b34c189a01a0787879cc4205dd8a1312dff141d06f284f6a1eb2b7c91e98cfb564@95.179.183.132:30303"]' > static-nodes.json && docker run -d --name bac-node --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -p 127.0.0.1:8545:8545 -v "$PWD":/w hyperledger/besu:24.12.2 --data-path=/w/data --genesis-file=/w/genesis.json --static-nodes-file=/w/static-nodes.json --sync-mode=FULL --sync-min-peers=1 --rpc-http-enabled --rpc-http-host=0.0.0.0 --host-allowlist='*'
Copy

Once it has synced, point the curl command above at http://127.0.0.1:8545 and compare it block by block with the public RPC.

Tested: using only the public genesis and node address, a fresh node synced from block 0 to the chain head in 24 seconds, and its block 10000 hash matched the project node.

A read-only node earns nothing; staking as a validator and sharing gas fees open after launch.

Every live figure on this page is read by your browser directly from the public RPC above (and from the indexer API on the same host). If all you see is “Loading…”, your tool did not run JavaScript.

The limits, stated plainly: both RPC addresses above reach the same project node on the same server, and that node is also the only block producer; in the first version block production, the relay and the indexer all sit in our single trust domain. A read-only node you run yourself can check that history has not been rewritten, but it cannot change who produces the blocks.
